thread:
ben: Heads up — after the handoff change we rolled last night I'm seeing a 15-30% p99 increase on multi-token chat paths. Suspect batching split or KV drain timing. Anyone else?

oliver: Yep noticed the same on staging. p50 fine, p99 jumps with >8 tokens. Looks correlated with `kv_cache` activity spikes.

sree: Posted profiling from a reproducer earlier. Kernel selection switches more often now because decode batches vary length more w/ separation. That churn is adding kernel load.

perf-bot: @channel perf snapshot: before= p99 230ms, after= p99 275ms. Throughput stable. Kernel timeline (median of samples): matmul 120ms -> 165ms, softmax 18ms -> 26ms, kv-ops 12ms -> 42ms.

ben: Interesting — kv ops jumped a lot. Could be KV eviction/restore thrash on handoff boundaries.

anna: Also saw more small decode batches getting scheduled immediately, which prevents good matmul packing. Prefill used to aggregate token budgets across in-flight requests; with the split we're losing that.

maria: Quick repro notes: run chat-repro with seeds 12/34, model=redwood-open-7b, concurrency 64, avg request tokens 12. Clear KV cache between runs to see the drain effect.

sree: Dumped queue metrics: prefill queue depth down ~40%, decode queue count up ~55%, average decode batch size down from 18->9. Token budget target for decode currently 64, prefill 256.

kevin: My hypothesis: the scheduler is favoring low-latency decode dispatch (decode-weight high), which starves prefill batching and reduces kernel packing efficiency. Also KV cache gets evicted more often when prefill backlog shrinks.

oliver: We could try two quick experiments:
1) Increase decode token_budget target slightly so decode batches hold longer before dispatch. 2) Add a transient KV-drain throttle window at handoff to avoid eviction churn.

ben: Agree. Want to try config change A then B. Proposed patch in runtime-configs branch: `batching-handoff-tweaks`.

sree: Proposed config snippet I'm going to try locally:

```
queue_policy:
  prefill_dispatch_delay_ms: 12
  decode_dispatch_delay_ms: 45
  prefill_token_budget: 220
  decode_token_budget: 96
  decode_min_batch: 8
  prefill_min_batch: 12
kv_cache:
  drain_threshold: 0.7
  drain_cooldown_ms: 250
  preserve_on_handoff: true
```

sree: Notes: increasing `decode_dispatch_delay_ms` gives decode more time to coalesce variable-length requests. `preserve_on_handoff` prevents eager eviction for short windows.

perf-bot: ran synthetic with sree's config: p99 dropped to 245ms (was 275). decode batch size median => 13, prefill => 16. KV op time reduced to ~22ms.

maria: Nice improvement. Any regression on cold-start or latency tail for single-token prompts?

sree: Single-token latencies increased ~4-6ms in microbenchmarks because of decode delay. But overall user-facing p99 better for multi-token chats which is our main SLO.

kevin: We should tune kernel selection too — the runtime recompile heuristic decides to use int8 matmul variant if avg seq_len < 32, but with mixed batches it flips. We might bias kernel choice based on dominant batch size rather than instantaneous.

oliver: Good call. Add a smoothing window to kernel selector (ema over batch sizes). Also fallback to safer kernel when churn detected.

ben: Plan: (1) land sree's queue+kv config as experiment behind flag on staging; (2) add kernel selector smoothing PR; (3) run 24h canary and collect p50/p95/p99 + kv evictions. If stable, promote.

anna: I'll add an eval script to nightly that simulates mixed-length chat traffic and emits kernel-switch counts.

maria: Can someone add a dashboard panel showing kernel-switch rate + kv-evict rate side-by-side? That correlation will help.

kevin: I'll add it to the runtime dashboards. Also adding alert if kernel-switches/sec > 5 and p99 > baseline.

ben: Thanks all. Let's reconvene after a 6-hour run. @sree can you post perf-bot snapshots in this thread when you have them? :thumbsup:

sree: Will do — starting canary now.

perf-bot: Canary run initial: p99=242ms, p95=88ms, kernel-switches=3/min, kv-evict-rate=0.04/sec. I'll post updates every 30m.

ben: Great, closing the loop later. If anyone sees regressions on low-token interactive workloads ping me directly.
